contract_plain_english: [PDF page 20; printed page 31, Exercise 2.6.9, read with PDF page 19; printed page 30, Lemma 2.6.8 and Equation (2.19)] Produce at least one sub-gaussian real random variable whose psi-two norm strictly increases when its mean is subtracted. This shows that the universal psi-two centering estimate from Lemma 2.6.8 needs a constant larger than one in general, in contrast to the coefficient-one L2 estimate (2.19).

source_evidence.observation: The exercise asks to show that the centering inequality in Lemma 2.6.8, unlike Equation (2.19), does not hold when its absolute constant C is set equal to 1.
The comparison inequality for the L2 norm is ||X - E X||_L2 <= ||X||_L2, so its multiplicative constant is exactly one.
For every sub-gaussian random variable X, the centered random variable X - E X is sub-gaussian and satisfies ||X - E X||_psi2 <= C ||X||_psi2 for an absolute constant C.
The sub-gaussian norm is defined by ||X||_psi2 = inf {t > 0 : E exp(X^2/t^2) <= 2}.

binders: [PDF page 20; printed page 31, Exercise 2.6.9; PDF page 19; printed page 30, Lemma 2.6.8] A real-valued random variable X, on an implicit probability space, is to be exhibited as a counterexample.
conclusions: [PDF page 20; printed page 31, Exercise 2.6.9] There exists a sub-gaussian random variable X for which ||X - E X||_psi2 > ||X||_psi2; equivalently, the universal centering bound ||X - E X||_psi2 <= ||X||_psi2 obtained by setting C = 1 in Lemma 2.6.8 is false.
definitions_and_conventions: [PDF page 16; printed page 27, Definition 2.5.6 and Equation (2.13)] ||X||_psi2 denotes inf {t > 0 : E exp(X^2/t^2) <= 2}, and a random variable having finite such norm is sub-gaussian in the stated equivalent sense.
[PDF page 19; printed page 30, Section 2.6.1 and Lemma 2.6.8] Centering means replacing X by X - E X.
[PDF page 19; printed page 30, footnote 5 attached to Lemma 2.6.8] An absolute constant is a numerical constant independent of the random variable under consideration.
hypotheses: [PDF page 20; printed page 31, Exercise 2.6.9 referring to Lemma 2.6.8] The exhibited random variable X is sub-gaussian.
implicit_context: [PDF page 19; printed page 30, Lemma 2.6.8] The centering inequality under discussion has the same psi-two norm on both sides and concerns all sub-gaussian random variables.
[PDF page 19; printed page 30, Equation (2.19); PDF page 20; printed page 31, Exercise 2.6.9] The contrast is with the L2 centering inequality, for which the coefficient one bound does hold.
[PDF page 20; printed page 31, Exercise 2.6.9] No particular distribution or probability space is prescribed; choosing a counterexample is part of the exercise.

details: [PDF page 20; printed page 31, Exercise 2.6.9] Saying the Lemma 2.6.8 inequality does not hold with C = 1 requires an existential counterexample to the corresponding universal coefficient-one bound.
[PDF page 20; printed page 31, Exercise 2.6.9] The counterexample must produce strict norm growth after centering: ||X - E X||_psi2 > ||X||_psi2.
[PDF page 19; printed page 30, Lemma 2.6.8] The variable witnessing failure belongs to the class of sub-gaussian random variables.
[PDF page 16; printed page 27, Equation (2.13)] The norm definition is expressed using X^2 and E exp(X^2/t^2), hence the source is working with real-valued random variables.
[PDF page 19; printed page 30, Lemma 2.6.8] The centered quantity is exactly X - E X.
[PDF page 16; printed page 27, Equation (2.13); PDF page 19; printed page 30, Lemma 2.6.8] Both sides of the inequality use the psi-two norm as defined by the exponential-moment threshold 2.
[PDF page 19; printed page 30, Lemma 2.6.8 and footnote 5] Lemma 2.6.8 asserts a bound with some absolute constant C.
[PDF page 20; printed page 31, Exercise 2.6.9] The exercise rejects only the specialization C = 1; it does not ask for the optimal valid absolute constant.

undebatable_constraints: [PDF page 20; printed page 31, Exercise 2.6.9] The result must refute the coefficient-one psi-two centering inequality, not merely restate the existence of a bound with an unspecified absolute constant.
[PDF page 19; printed page 30, Lemma 2.6.8; PDF page 20; printed page 31, Exercise 2.6.9] The witness must be a sub-gaussian random variable and must compare X - E X against that same X.
[PDF page 16; printed page 27, Definition 2.5.6 and Equation (2.13)] The norm being compared is the psi-two norm defined by the exponential-moment condition with threshold 2.

[PDF page 20; printed page 31, Exercise 2.6.9] Failure with C = 1 means an actual counterexample satisfying ||X - E X||_psi2 > ||X||_psi2; a claim that the coefficient-one inequality has not been proved is insufficient.
[PDF page 20; printed page 31, Exercise 2.6.9] The source does not require determining the best constant C or classifying all counterexamples.
